title: How Atomic Clocks Define the Second
description: How cesium atoms define the second and why atomic clocks are so accurate, from NIST and NASA.
narration: How do we measure a single second so precisely? Atomic clocks are the most accurate way to measure time. Inside, waves are aimed at cesium atoms, and the atoms absorb them and leap to a different energy level. That jump only happens at one precise frequency. Cesium atoms respond to 9,192,631,770 wave cycles every second, so the second itself is defined as that many cycles. The best cesium clocks drift by only about a three-hundred-millionth of a second each year, while a quartz wristwatch may be off by about 15 seconds a month. Quartz clocks drift too: after six weeks, even good ones can be off by a full millisecond.
